messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: [SEV-2] Serving: multi-GPU collective failures detected in TP job pool - auto-escalating to on-call. Affected cluster: us-west-2-gpu-4. Symptom: repeated nccl communicator timeouts + container restarts. First observed: 2024-11-03T09:14:49Z. Link: https://ops.redwood/incident/4623456789

jess: saw the pager, I'm on it. can the oncall-ml confirm?

samir: oncall-ml here, grabbing details. which jobs impacted?

oncall-ml: getting list now. preliminary: 6 TP jobs failed across 3 nodes (gpu-node-17/18/21). Some batch inference customers saw 5-30% error spikes.

miguel: I see container restarts on node-18 around 09:12-09:16. kube events show OOMKilled and then CrashLoopBackOff for the serving-worker pods.

erin: support reporting customer tenant: tenant-acme had 12 failed requests, higher latency on streaming endpoints. notifying customers now.

dave: throwing early hypothesis: NCCL deadlocks due to intermittent node flaps + KV cache pressure? any Xid in dmesg?

gpu-sre-bot: ALERT: node-18 kernel log snippet: 
```
[  612.345678] NVRM: Xid (79): GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  612.345680] NVRM: GPU 0: GPU reported Xid 79, pid: 12345, name: python
[  613.001234] kubelet: Container runtime restarted container serving-worker-abc (exitCode=137)
[  613.100000] dockerd: oom-killer: killing process 12345 (python) total-vm: 5120000kB
```

jess: Xid79 + OOMKilled -> fits. Did we see NCCL errors in logs?

oncall-ml: yes, pod logs show repeated NCCL handshake timeouts and "unreachable rank" messages. snippet: 
```
[2024-11-03 09:12:55,234] ERROR: nccl: [Rank 1] NCCL WARN Timeout in allreduce: 2 retries
[2024-11-03 09:12:55,235] ERROR: communicator: rendezvous failed: timeout
[2024-11-03 09:12:55,236] ERROR: Runtime: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at forward()
```

samir: is this only TP (tensor parallel) or TP+PP mixes?

oncall-ml: primarily TP-only clusters, pipeline parallel jobs on different node pools unaffected so far.

miguel: node metrics show memory pressure on GPU0 on node-17 and 18. nvtop shows one process using >95% memory then OOM. Could be a memory leak or bad batching.

jess: quick mitigation options? reduce TP degree, fall back to single-GPU model variant, or restart pods one-by-one to drain bad state.

dave: also consider toggling NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING and NCCL_IB_TIMEOUT heuristics. but risky during live traffic.

erin: customers want ETA. we should communicate currently investigating, mitigation in progress, possible degraded traffic for 30-60m.

oncall-ml: immediate plan: 1) isolate the three nodes (cordon), 2) restart affected pods with SINGLE_GPU=true variant, 3) enable nccl async error env on restarts to allow graceful recovery, 4) monitor for recurrence. executing now.

jess: +1. cordon node-17/18/21 and scale down replicas on that pool. miguel can you run cordon?

miguel: cordoning nodes and draining non-critical pods. commands I ran: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
kubectl cordon gpu-node-18
kubectl cordon gpu-node-21
kubectl drain gpu-node-18 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

nginx-balance: (system message) shifting 30% of incoming requests off the TP pool to fallback instances.

oncall-ml: rolling restart serving-workers on remaining healthy nodes with env: NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 NCCL_IB_TIMEOUT=22. Also set REDWOOD_FALLBACK_SINGLE_GPU=true on restarted pods.

samir: logs after restart show fewer NCCL timeouts but still a couple of "unreachable peer" traces, likely because some jobs maintain stale communicators. we should forcibly kill long-running processes that started before restart.

jess: agreed. kill stale PIDs for serving-worker on drained nodes. miguel to confirm container restarted count.

miguel: containers restarted: node-17 (3), node-18 (4), node-21 (2). backfills running onto healthy nodes.

erin: customer update drafted: "We are investigating an infrastructure issue affecting multi-GPU inference. Some requests may fail or have increased latency. We have isolated affected hosts and are applying mitigations; updates in 30 minutes." sending now.

dave: can we collect core dumps / nccl debug traces for postmortem? enable NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and collect /var/log/nccl-*.

oncall-ml: enabling NCCL_DEBUG and adding a persistent sidecar to collect logs to s3: s3://redwood-incidents/4623456789/. also capturing GPU stats: `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION` every 5s for 5 minutes.

gpu-sre-bot: note: observed fabric link flaps on node-18 around 09:11 in IB counters (retry counters increase). could be intermittent NIC firmware hiccup. forwarding telemetry to infra.

jess: if fabric is flapping, that explains NCCL rendezvous failures. we should mark those nodes for deeper hardware inspection and move TP scheduling away until they pass health checks.

erin: support: customers with SLA seats (tenant-acme and tenant-zen) flagged for priority outreach. preparing targeted post-incident notes.

samir: for immediate risk reduction, temporarily set TP_MAX_DEGREE=1 for queued TP jobs and add a pre-flight check to reject TP placement on nodes with IB retry > 100 in last 5m. I'll open a short-lived feature flag.

oncall-ml: mitigation executed: nodes cordoned + restarts with fallback + NCCL debug enabled. after 18 minutes error rate down to baseline. no new Xid79s in last 10 minutes.

miguel: hardware team accepted follow-up: they'll reseat NIC and run firmware health check on node-18 during maintenance window. marking nodes for postmortem.

jess: handoff to infra and postmortem owner: samir (lead), miguel (hardware), oncall-ml (runtime analysis), erin (customer comms). next steps: collect logs, confirm whether root cause was NIC fabric flaps causing NCCL timeouts and then OOM on falling processes.

dave: reminder: include timeline, metrics (errors/sec, latency P95), pod restart counts, Xid occurrences, and kernel dmesg in the postmortem.

oncall-ml: creating incident ticket: INC-4623456789 and assigning. ETA for initial postmortem draft: EOD.

erin: update to customers: "We mitigated the issue by isolating affected hosts and routing traffic to healthy capacity. We're investigating root cause; we'll follow up with a detailed incident report." sent.

gpu-sre-bot: STATE: mitigations stable, monitoring for 60m. set pager to quiet for this thread.

jess: thanks all. if error rate creeps up, page 2: oncall-sre. otherwise will transition to postmortem work. :thumbsup:

end of thread.
